notices.text: All data in this demo is made up and generated by fgaudit itself.

findings.title: Interfaces port2 and port6 have overlapping subnets
findings.detail: interface port2 (10.10.0.0/24, VDOM root) and interface port6 (10.10.0.128/25, VDOM root) overlap in 10.10.0.128/25. Connected routes for the same addresses on two interfaces make forwarding and replies unpredictable. The VDOM has allow-subnet-overlap enabled.
findings.next_step: Give one of the interfaces a non-overlapping subnet, or document why the overlap is intended.

findings.title: DHCP range 1 (port2) overlaps the subnet of port6
findings.detail: DHCP range 1 (port2) (10.10.0.100-10.10.0.199, VDOM root) and interface port6 (10.10.0.128/25, VDOM root) overlap in 10.10.0.128-10.10.0.199. Leased addresses would also belong to another connected network.
findings.next_step: Correct the DHCP range or the interface subnet.

findings.title: IPsec remote network partner-p2 overlaps local interface vlan100
findings.detail: phase 2 remote selector partner-p2 (10.30.0.0/24, VDOM root) and interface vlan100 (10.30.0.0/24, VDOM root) overlap in 10.30.0.0/24. Traffic to these addresses stays local (connected route) instead of entering the tunnel. A remote selector that is a larger summary of a local network is not reported.
findings.next_step: Renumber one side or use NAT over the tunnel.

findings.title: Policy 20 "block-guest-smtp" can never match: 40 "lan-any-out" above it catches the same traffic with a different action
findings.detail: Policy 40 "lan-any-out" (action accept) fully covers policy 20 "block-guest-smtp" (action deny) in every match criterion: interfaces, source, destination, service, schedule, users. Traffic meant for 20 "block-guest-smtp" gets action accept instead. Note: policy 40 has the higher ID but sits higher in the list (position 15 before 16). Order counts, not the ID.
findings.next_step: Decide which action is intended. If the later policy should apply, move it above the earlier one. Check the hit count and last-used time of both policies on the FortiGate (Policy & Objects > Firewall Policy) before you change or delete anything.

findings.title: DHCP range 2 (port3) lies partly outside its interface subnet
findings.detail: DHCP range 2 (port3) (10.20.0.200-10.20.1.20, VDOM root) and interface port3 (10.20.0.0/24, VDOM root) overlap in 10.20.1.0-10.20.1.20. Clients would get addresses that the interface cannot reach directly. The range shown is the part outside.
findings.next_step: Align the DHCP range with the interface subnet.

findings.title: IP pools wan-pool and wan-pool-2 overlap
findings.detail: IP pool wan-pool (203.0.113.3-203.0.113.4, VDOM root) and IP pool wan-pool-2 (203.0.113.4/31, VDOM root) overlap in 203.0.113.4. Two NAT pools hand out the same addresses, which can cause session clashes.
findings.next_step: Make the pools disjoint, or use one pool.

findings.title: VIPs web-vip and old-web-vip claim the same external address
findings.detail: VIP external IP web-vip (203.0.113.2, VDOM root) and VIP external IP old-web-vip (203.0.113.2, VDOM root) overlap in 203.0.113.2. Both VIPs match the same external IP and ports on the same interface, so only one can take effect.
findings.next_step: Use different external IPs or non-overlapping ports.

findings.title: Policy 41 "staff-https" is redundant: 4 "lan-web-out" above it covers it with the same action
findings.detail: Policy 4 "lan-web-out" covers policy 41 "staff-https" in every match criterion and has the same action (accept). 41 "staff-https" never receives traffic. Security profiles differ (later -> earlier policy): av-profile: strict-av -> -; ssl-ssh-profile: - -> certificate-inspection; webfilter-profile: - -> default.
findings.next_step: Check whether the later policy can be removed. If the security profiles differ, the earlier policy's profiles are the ones applied. Check the hit count and last-used time of both policies on the FortiGate (Policy & Objects > Firewall Policy) before you change or delete anything.

findings.title: Policy 42 "lan-dns-ntp-copy" duplicates 6 "lan-dns-ntp"
findings.detail: Both policies have identical match criteria and the same action (accept). Only 6 "lan-dns-ntp" ever matches.
findings.next_step: Remove the duplicate only after comparing hit counts and security profiles. Check the hit count and last-used time of both policies on the FortiGate (Policy & Objects > Firewall Policy) before you change or delete anything.

summary.verdict: Overall change risk: HIGH. 7 finding(s): 4 high, 3 medium. + 5 INFO.

findings.title: Policy order changed: 4 "lan-web-out" now evaluated in a different order against policies with another action
findings.detail: Policy 4 "lan-web-out" moved from position 4 to 3. It can match the same traffic as 3 "printers-no-internet", which have a different action. The first match wins, so the behaviour changes.
findings.next_step: Confirm the new order is intended and test the affected traffic.

findings.title: Management access removed on interface port2
findings.detail: Removing https, ssh from allowaccess can lock you out if you manage the FortiGate through this interface. Changes: allowaccess: ping https ssh -> ping.
findings.next_step: Make sure you have another management path (console, other interface) before applying.

findings.title: Broad accept rule: policy 70 "temp-any"
findings.detail: The policy accepts traffic with 'any' in source, destination, service.
findings.next_step: Narrow source, destination or service, and confirm the rule was intended.

findings.title: Default route 1 changed
findings.detail: The default route carries all traffic without a more specific route, including your remote management session. Changes: gateway: 203.0.113.1 -> 203.0.113.6.
findings.next_step: Apply with console access and check the new gateway and distance.

findings.title: Unencrypted management protocol enabled on port1
findings.detail: http sends credentials in clear text. Changes: allowaccess: ping -> ping http.
findings.next_step: Use HTTPS/SSH only, or restrict trusted hosts.

findings.title: Object web-srv changed
findings.detail: Objects change the behaviour of every policy that uses them. Changes: subnet: 10.20.0.10 255.255.255.255 -> 10.20.0.12 255.255.255.255. Affected policies: 1 "lan-to-dmz-web".
findings.next_step: Review the affected policies.

findings.title: Logging disabled on policy 2 "lan-to-mail"
findings.detail: Without traffic logs you cannot trace or prove what this policy allowed. Changes: logtraffic: all -> disable.
findings.next_step: Keep at least logtraffic utm or all unless there is a documented reason.

findings.title: Encrypted value in system admin [admin] not comparable
findings.detail: The encrypted (ENC) value of password differs. FortiOS can encrypt the same secret differently in each backup, so fgaudit cannot tell whether it changed. This is not a confirmation that nothing changed.
findings.next_step: If the secret should be unchanged, confirm it another way (for example, the tunnel or login still works).
